authors: design agent for LEAD-STR-class-group-ecdlp-bridge (unfrozen draft; freeze and approval belong to the Coordinator)

links.note: Design only. Two sub-minute PARI/GP feasibility probes (existence of toy parameter families) were run and are reported in design.md as probes, not results. No battery data exists.

question: On toy prime-order curves with N not dividing p^j-1 for j<=2, is every oracle in {endomorphism image, class-group step and path with level structure, E[ell] torsion evaluation, Miller value and its N-th root, and their joint use} indistinguishable, by a fixed battery of eight transcript distinguishers, from a lazy generic-group simulator that has no point or coordinate of the curve, while the battery flags four known leaking oracles and does not flag a pure group-law oracle?

claims.text: Positive-control validity: the battery flags every designated (control, distinguisher) cell of the four positive controls on all three size bands, and its minimum detectable dilution is reported per distinguisher.
Negative-control validity and calibration: the pure group-law oracle, the value-shuffled Miller oracle and both A/A pairs produce no flagged cell at the family-wise level.

On the test family, no k-mixed cell (oracle by distinguisher) among the tested oracle set is flagged: the tested oracles are simulable by S0 at the tested depth and query budget (closure for the tested set only).
claims.if_supported: closure of the tested oracle set at depth <= the battery's stated bidegree and for query budget sqrt(N)/4; the simulation lemma named by the lead's next_action has an empirical no-counterexample record for these oracles and still needs the written proof
claims.if_not_supported: a flagged cell is a candidate non-simulable identity: a candidate real lead, to be replicated on holdout curves and then priced separately

claims.text: k-free structure inventory: the set of k-free cells flagged is reported; a flagged k-free cell refutes the lead's literal inventory of identities (reciprocity constants only) for that oracle but carries no information about k.
The battery makes no statement about oracles outside the set, identities above the stated degree, query budgets above sqrt(N)/4 for k-mixed queries, N above 2^20, or any asymptotic exponent.

hypotheses.statement: For every tested oracle o and distinguisher d, real transcripts and S0 transcripts are exchangeable within curve strata (lead disposition: closure at exponent 1/2 for the family).
hypotheses.mechanism: End(G)=Z/N (O1), transport preserves k (T1), ell-torsion data are k-independent (O3), and with N not dividing p-1 every Miller value is an N-th power so only reciprocity constants relate values (the lead's claim, unverified).

predictions.minimum_effect: 0 of 72 k-mixed cells flagged after Bonferroni at alpha 0.01 over 144 cells, replicated on holdout curves if any
all designated positive-control cells flagged in 3 of 3 bands
0 flagged among negative-control and A/A cells

at least one k-free cell flagged for T6/T7 or T5, because the lead's own K2 formula U(iP)=c r_i C^(i/N) is a k-free algebraic structure; stated as an expectation of the lead's analysis, not of the closure

hypotheses.statement: At least one tested oracle has a k-mixed identity that S0 cannot satisfy (the lead is not closed for that oracle).
hypotheses.mechanism: A Miller value, transport datum or torsion evaluation that depends on coordinates of aP+bQ in a way not fixed by reciprocity, scalar action or the class-group relation lattice.

predictions.minimum_effect: >= 1 replicated k-mixed cell on the test family, after the gates pass

arms.description: Lazy generic-group simulator S0: random injective labels, formal linear-form table over the unknown scalar, receives only N, p, the public scalars of the oracle language (endomorphism eigenvalue, class-group cycle scalars, reciprocity-symmetry rule) and no point or coordinate of E
Real oracles T1-T7 and the joint oracle T9 implemented on the toy curve, labels through a random injective relabelling of G (and of each transported G')
Real pure group-law oracle T0 on the same instances: sets the collision and label-equality floor common to every arm
A/A on the simulator side: an independent second draw of S0 (fresh seeds, same public inputs)
A/A on the real side: transcripts from a second independent draw of (P,k) and query seeds on the same curves
Anomalous curve (N = p), oracle = p-adic elliptic logarithm value in F_p (additive homomorphism G -> F_p); same code path as T6/T7 value oracles
N | p-1 (cofactor 2, 27 such curves found below 60000 in a probe), same Miller loop as T6, final exponent (p-1)/N: reduced Tate self-pairing, bilinear
Supersingular y^2=x^3+x, N | p+1, reduced Tate pairing with distortion map (embedding degree 2); log taken in mu_N

x-coordinate oracle on the test family: non-homomorphic but algebraic (x(2R) = rational function of x(R)); shows the relation distinguishers fire on a non-additive identity, which is the shape a Miller-value identity would have
Titration: PADIC oracle with probability eps in {1/4,1/16,1/64} replaced by a uniform value; gives the minimum detectable leak per distinguisher
Pure group-law oracle T0 versus simulator S0, matched on curves, seeds and query plan
Real T6/T7 values with the value-to-label assignment replaced by a seeded random function (same marginal, structure destroyed), as in harness/ctrl_valueshuffle.py

positive.expected_detection: p-anom: D3,D4,D6,D7 flagged; p-tate1 and p-tate2: D3,D4,D6 (and D7 for tate1); p-xcoord: D7 only (D3 and D4 must NOT flag, which shows the relation test is not a homomorphism test in disguise); p-dilute: report the smallest eps flagged per distinguisher

null_population.description: Pure group-law transcripts (arm n-pure) and Miller-oracle transcripts with value-to-label structure destroyed by a seeded random function (arm n-shuffle), both on the 18 test-family curves
null_population.generator: n-pure: real T0 oracle vs S0 under the shared query plan; n-shuffle: T6/T7 outputs replaced by SHA-256(seed, label-form) mapped uniformly into F_p^*, preserving the marginal
null_population.why_n: 18 curves x 64 transcripts per world, the same size as the test arm, so the negative cells have the same resolution as the test cells

factors.name: curve
factors.how: 6 curves per size band drawn by the recipe in design.md from seeds derived from the protocol hash; identical curve set in both worlds (strata)

factors.name: size_band
factors.how: N in [2^12,2^14), [2^14,2^17), [2^17,2^20]; all arms run in every band

factors.name: planted_scalar_and_generator
factors.how: P a uniform generator and k uniform in [1,N-1] per transcript, from the per-transcript seed, independent of world

factors.name: query_plan
factors.how: query forms aP+bQ drawn from the frozen plan generator by seed; the same plan is replayed in both worlds

factors.name: label_encoding
factors.how: fresh random injective relabelling per transcript in both worlds; labels carry no arithmetic

factors.name: query_budget
factors.value: k_mixed: floor(sqrt(N)/4) distinct forms per transcript; k_free: 512
factors.how: keeps the instance-dependent coincidence term q^2/(2N) below 1/32 in k-mixed transcripts

factors.name: miller_normalisation
factors.value: f_{N,T} normalised at O by the uniformiser x/y; queries with R in {O,T} answered 'undefined' in both worlds
factors.how: the normalisation constant is part of the oracle language; S0 is given the same rule

factors.name: binary
factors.how: one binary, sha256 pinned at freeze, single thread

factors.name: permutation_seed
factors.how: derived from the protocol hash and cell id

factors.name: host_load
factors.how: no clock is read; host facts recorded only

seed_derivation.note: curve, transcript, query-plan, relabelling and permutation seeds are SHA-256 of (protocol sha256, role string, band, curve index, transcript index); holdout curves use a second role string drawn only after the discovery analysis is filed

instance_sampling.rule: per band the 6 curves are the first 6 hits of a seed-ordered scan over primes p in the band and coefficients (a,b) satisfying the admission predicate in design.md; no curve is dropped after construction except by the stated admission predicate

blinding.how: experiment_protocol.py blind masks arm names and control roles; the analyst sees cells as A..L until the positive-control gate and A/A gate are evaluated by the frozen script
blinding.unmasked_at: after the analysis script has written gate_verdicts.json

power.note: 144 cells = 9 oracles x 8 distinguishers x 2 query classes (inapplicable cells count, which is conservative). Per cell the statistic is a within-curve stratified label permutation with 199999 resamples; add-one doubled-tail minimum 2/(199999+1)=1e-5 against alpha/m=0.01/144=6.94e-5. Instances: 54 = 18 test-family curves (3 bands x 6) + 36 control-family curves (AN, K1, K2: 3 bands x 4 curves each). Per curve and world 64 transcripts. Resolution is arithmetic only; power to detect a leak of size eps is not claimed beyond the titration arm's measured minimum detectable dilution, reported per distinguisher; D6 and D7 are exact all-or-nothing relation tests with no graded power.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: estimate from sizing, not measured: ~12 arms x 18-54 curves x 64 transcripts x (512 + sqrt(N)/4 queries) at about 5 microseconds per field-level oracle step plus 144 x 199999 permutations of 1152 values; to be replaced by a one-call timing before freeze

primary.name: flagged cells
primary.definition: number of (oracle, distinguisher, query class) cells with permutation p <= alpha/m, per arm group

primary.name: cell p-value
primary.definition: add-one doubled-tail stratified permutation p of the per-transcript statistic, real minus simulator, 199999 resamples
primary.formula: (1 + #{resamples with |T*| >= |T_obs|}) / (199999 + 1) with T the stratified mean difference; doubled-tail convention

primary.name: oracle cost
primary.unit: counted units: group_add + group_dbl + group_neg (each 1) ; F_p mul, sqr, inv separately; Miller_iter (each charged as its measured F_p mul/sqr/inv); isogeny_eval (charged as its F_p ops)
primary.definition: every oracle query from request to answer, by kind; label canonicalisation and relabelling are uncharged and listed as counters

secondary.name: minimum detectable dilution
secondary.definition: smallest eps in the titration grid flagged in >= 90 percent of the 64-transcript replicate draws, per distinguisher
secondary.formula: min over the eps grid of eps such that the flagged fraction over 64-transcript replicate draws is >= 0.9

secondary.name: standardised effect
secondary.unit: sd of the per-transcript statistic under S0
secondary.definition: (mean real - mean sim) / pooled sd, stratified by curve
secondary.formula: sum over curves of (mean_real - mean_sim) weights / pooled sd under S0, weights proportional to transcripts per curve

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: all planned (arm, curve, transcript) cells executed, then stop; no interim look at any p-value
holdout replication of any flagged cell on 18 fresh curves is a single pre-specified second stage, run once
if the positive-control gate or the A/A gate fails, stop: the run is invalid_measurement and no oracle verdict is read

invalidation_rules: a transcript whose oracle answers fail the checker's independent recomputation is a refuted row, excluded from nothing: it voids the run until the implementation is fixed by amendment before any other data are read
a curve failing the admission predicate is replaced by the next scan hit; the rejection is logged
a cell with fewer than 48 usable transcripts per world in some curve is reported as not_evaluable and counted as not flagged only for family size, never as support

decision_rule.text: Gates first. Gate G1 (positive): every designated positive-control cell flagged at p <= alpha/m on all three bands. Gate G2 (negative and A/A): no negative-control or A/A cell flagged. If G1 or G2 fails the verdict is invalid_measurement. Otherwise on the test family: if no k-mixed cell is flagged, C3 is supported within scope (closure for the tested oracle set and depth only); if k-mixed cell(s) are flagged, each must replicate on 18 holdout curves at alpha 0.01 (one test) with the same sign and an effect of at least 0.5 sd or an exact relation in >= 90 percent of transcripts; a replicated cell is a candidate non-simulable identity. k-free flags are reported under C4 and do not change the verdict on C3.
decision_rule.statistic: per-transcript scalar for the distinguisher, mean difference real minus simulator, label permutation within curve strata
decision_rule.interval: 99 percent bootstrap over curves for the standardised effect; exact for relation distinguishers
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: standardised mean difference in sd units, and for D6/D7/D8 the fraction of transcripts showing the exact relation

graphs: cell p-value heat map (oracle by distinguisher, k-free and k-mixed panels) with the Bonferroni line and positive-control rows
titration curve: detection rate against eps per distinguisher

inadmissible: adding, removing or reparametrising a distinguisher, a degree bound or a query budget after any transcript was read
dropping a curve or band because its cells flag or fail to flag; replacing a curve outside the admission predicate
reading a cell p-value without the gate verdicts, or reading the test family before G1 and G2 are evaluated on controls
calling the result a proof of the simulation lemma, an exponent, or a statement about any oracle outside the tested set
treating a k-free flag as an ECDLP lead, or a null as closure of identities above the tested degree or of query budgets above sqrt(N)/4
building a second simulator S1 that encodes a flagged identity and re-running the same cell as if it were the original test (that is a new protocol)
using wall time anywhere in a decision

literature.claim: jet and endomorphism oracles classified GGM-simulable by an analytic specification test; this protocol is an empirical transcript battery, a different instrument
incidence and endomorphism-image oracles simulable; the elliptic-net and jet oracles recorded non-simulable but DLP-equivalent

literature.ref: Shoup, Lower Bounds for Discrete Logarithms and Related Problems, EUROCRYPT 1997
literature.claim: generic simulation error O(q^2/N), which fixes the k-mixed query budget

literature.ref: Duman, Hartmann, Kiltz, Kunzweiler, Lehmann, Riepel, Generic models for group actions, PKC 2023
literature.claim: generic group action model with a lower bound; models the action alone, not an action on curves carrying a generic group
